title: I have thousands of transactions and don't know how much I've made
excerpt: Portfolios with tens or hundreds of thousands of transactions spread across exchanges, wallets and chains. How they are cleaned up, reconciled and turned into a figure you can stand behind.

hero.h1: You have so many transactions you've lost count
hero.subheading: You may trade on several chains, hold half a dozen wallets, have part of your history on exchanges that no longer exist, and find that much of what shows up at your addresses is spam you never asked for. Before calculating any tax, you need to work out what actually happened.

sections.entrada: Figures from a real multi-chain portfolio. They are not your specific case, but they show why a spreadsheet won't solve this.

sections.body:
You started on an exchange, then opened a wallet, then tried a new chain because the fees were lower, then got into a couple of protocols. Each step made sense on its own. Taken together, it is now a jumble of data scattered across places with different formats.

You've tried to put it in order. You probably ran everything through a tool and it gave you a gain you don't recognise, or it simply choked on the volume.

The problem isn't a tax problem yet. It's a data problem: until you know which transactions really happened, which were transfers between your own accounts and what cost to give to anything you received without buying it, there is no figure to calculate. That groundwork is exactly what we do.

steps.title: An inventory of sources before touching anything
steps.body: Which exchanges, which wallets, which chains, which periods. This gives a list of what is there and what is missing, and it's the first thing we show you: knowing what you don't have matters as much as processing what you do.

steps.title: Normalisation
steps.body: Formats, asset naming, time zones and decimal precision. Without this, transactions end up in the wrong order and the FIFO calculation goes wrong with them.

steps.title: Identifying internal transfers
steps.body: We establish who owns each destination address, to separate what was a sale from what was simply moving funds to yourself. This is where most of the phantom gain sits.

steps.title: Filtering spam with judgement
steps.body: Not with an automatic blacklist: some junk tokens look legitimate and some real transactions look like junk. Every doubtful case is examined.

steps.title: Tax classification and manual review
steps.body: Each transaction is given its tax treatment. Anything no rule resolves with certainty is set aside and reviewed by hand, and the decision is documented.

steps.title: Calculation and traceability
steps.body: The FIFO rule applied to the reconciled portfolio, with the per-transaction detail behind every total.

sections.entrada: A summary that fits on one screen, with all the detail underneath.

bullets: Exports from every exchange you have used, even if they are incomplete or split across several periods.
Read-only API keys where possible: they avoid manual export errors. Never private keys.
Public addresses for all your wallets, including ones you no longer use. Without them, internal transfers cannot be identified.
Which chains and protocols you have used, even if only roughly and from memory.
Bank statements showing euros in and out, which anchor the reconstruction to something verifiable.
Any previous report you have generated, even if the numbers don't add up. It saves time.

items.q: Is there a limit on the number of transactions?
items.a: Not on volume. The hard cases aren't the large ones, they're the scattered ones: small protocols with no maintained explorer, poorly documented chains or closed platforms. If your case includes any of those, we tell you before we start.

It depends far more on the state of the data than on the amount. A large but orderly portfolio moves quickly; a medium-sized one with gaps to reconstruct can take weeks. After the inventory phase we give you a specific timeframe, because any estimate before that would be guesswork.

The portfolio is rebuilt from the start of your activity, not from the tax year you want to declare: without the earlier history there is no reliable acquisition cost. If this reveals tax years that were declared incorrectly, we tell you and look at regularising them with you.

items.q: Next year, does it all have to be done again?
items.a: No. We hand over the reconciled portfolio, which is the clean starting point for the following tax years. The heavy lifting is done once.

It is based on volume and, above all, on the number of sources and the state they arrive in. Once we have seen a sample, we give you a price before starting. Timeframes and prices are estimates that depend on the complexity of the portfolio.

cierre.h2: Let's start by finding out what's there
cierre.body: Tell us roughly how many transactions you have, which exchanges and chains you have used and which tax years concern you. That tells us the size of the job, and we'll give you an indicative timeframe and price.
